transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Ravi Kumar (CTO - Ironbridge), Elise Park (Head of InfoSec), Jonas Lee (DevOps), Marta Ruiz (Legal)

Agenda:
- Quick intros and objectives
- Compliance posture (SOC2, ISO, HIPAA)
- Deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/on-prem)
- KMS/BYOK and HSM requirements
- Audit logs, retention, RBAC, SSO/SAML/SCIM
- Next steps and timeline

Summary:
Ironbridge is evaluating Redwood for a clinical notes ingestion product that will process PHI. Primary concerns: SOC2 Type II evidence, HIPAA BAAs, BYOK/HSM integration for key separation, audit log retention (13+ months), fine-grained RBAC, and SSO/SAML with Okta + SCIM. They prefer a Private deployment but want cost and latency tradeoffs vs Dedicated. They asked for benchmark windows and a technical deep dive for Dedicated.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena, AE at Redwood. Quick roll call real fast, and then Marcus will jump into the security details.
[00:18] Ravi: Hi, Ravi here. CTO at Ironbridge. We've got Elise, Jonas and Marta on. Thanks for fitting us in.
[00:26] Elise: Hi all. Elise, InfoSec. We want to make sure any provider meets HIPAA and our internal ISO-ish controls, right.
[00:34] Marcus: Great. I'll give an overview of our security posture, the hosted/dedicated/private options, and dig into KMS/HSM and audit logs. Apologies if some product names get mangled, transcription sometimes swaps things.
[00:48] Jonas: No problem. We mostly want to understand what we can control — keys, logging, data residency, latency.
[00:55] Lena: Top-level ask for today: confirm compliance artifacts we can provision, what Private looks like network-wise, and high-level pricing signals.
[01:10] Marcus: Okay quick baseline — Redwood has SOC 2 type II, and we've got an ISO 27001 mapped control set. We can furnish the report under NDA. For PHI we'll do BAAs for Private and Dedicated customers; Hosted has a managed offering but we need to confirm scope.
[01:30] Elise: When you say hosted, do you support HIPAA covered workloads? We read some docs but need specifics.
[01:38] Marcus: Short answer: Hosted can support it for some customers but typically Ironbridge-level PHI wants private control plane or dedicated with BAA, because of data separation and audit expectations. "Hosted" in our docs sometimes implies multi-tenant control plane. We do have enterprise-hosted variants but let's map to your risk appetite.
[01:55] Elise: Ok, that's helpful. We require isolated logging and the ability to export logs to our SIEM. Retention for audit logs is 13 months minimum, ideally 24 for certain flows.
[02:08] Marcus: We retain request-level traces for 90 days by default, but for enterprise we can configure export and longer retention. For Private deployments you can host logs in your own S3 or SIEM via connectors, and set retention per policy.
[02:22] Ravi: On keys — we plan to require BYOK and HSM-backed keys in AWS KMS or an HSM appliance in our VPC. How tight is the integration?
[02:31] Marcus: We support BYOK with cloud KMS providers — AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS — and can work with HSMs via a proxy. For Private we can integrate with your KMS over VPC peering or proxy. There's also an option for on-prem HSM if you want full custody.
[02:45] Jonas: Sounds good. Does Redwood ever see plaintext model inputs? We need to understand where PHI is traversing.
[02:52] Marcus: At a high level the runtime processes tokenized inputs on GPUs — we don't persist inputs unless caching or logs are enabled. For Dedicated/Private you control cache storage and can disable prefix caching for PHI. Hosted may buffer or cache per performance profiles; we can disable that for regulated streams.
[03:08] Elise: Can you do token redaction or partial masking before logging?
[03:12] Marcus: We have filters and can redact at the edge via ingestion hooks; on Private you can run those in your VPC to avoid sending PHI to Redwood control plane. We also support structured output and functions to avoid free-form PHI in logs.
[03:29] Lena: Quick clarification: when Marcus says control plane, is that the management console?
[03:33] Marcus: Yes, control plane = console, model catalog and rollout logic. For Private there is an optional customer-controlled control plane — it's a hybrid; the data plane stays in your environment.
[03:42] Marta: Legals question — do you offer BAAs for Dedicated? You said yes, but how about Hosted?
[03:47] Marcus: We have BAAs for Dedicated and Private customers; Hosted BAAs are handled case-by-case and often require an enterprise contract. I'll flag legal for a follow-up.
[03:56] Jonas: On network side, for Private do you support VPC peering or PrivateLink? We prefer VPC endpoints for egress restrictions.
[04:03] Marcus: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and customers can deploy our runtime inside their VPC in the on-prem package. For Dedicated we usually set up VPC peering + NAT controls to allow secure routing.
[04:15] Elise: Authentication — we'd like SSO via Okta, SCIM provisioning and role-based access. Does Redwood do SAML and SCIM?
[04:22] Marcus: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. RBAC supports role templates and custom roles. We can map to your groups; for stricter setups you can integrate with your IdP and restrict admin actions to certain groups.
[04:35] Ravi: How granular is RBAC? Can we separate ability to change rollouts from ability to create models or see logs?
[04:41] Marcus: Yes. We have role primitives: Admin, Operator, Viewer, Billing, Model Onboarder. You can create custom roles that restrict model rollouts, secret access, and log viewing.
[04:52] Elise: Do audit logs capture token-level usage and admin actions? We need an immutable audit trail.
[04:58] Marcus: Admin actions and API keys are logged — user, action, timestamp, resource. For token-level usage, we log metadata (request size, model, latency) and pointer to content if logging is enabled. For PHI we recommend disabling content logging and exporting metadata only.
[05:16] Jonas: For Dedicated, what's the SLA and uptime commitments? We have strict availability windows for some workflows.
[05:22] Lena: Our Dedicated contracts include SLA terms; we'll share the standard SLA. SLA often varies by plan and reserved capacity. Marcus, do you want to add?
[05:29] Marcus: SLA is typically 99.9% for Dedicated, with options for higher depending on reserved configs. For Private on-prem it's customer responsibility, but we provide best-practice runbooks.
[05:40] Elise: Encryption at rest and in transit — standard? We need FIPS-compliant ciphers and keys under our KMS.
[05:47] Marcus: TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest; with BYOK you control the CMK. FIPS-compliant key stores can be supported via dedicated HSM integrations.
[05:58] Ravi: Can we get deterministic retention TTLs for challenge logs and model caches? We need to ensure deletion windows for data subject requests.
[06:06] Marcus: Yes, data lifecycle policies are configurable. For Private you can set cache TTLs and garbage collection windows. For Hosted we have retention tiers and can honor deletion requests via the support process.
[06:18] Elise: Do you have a documented vulnerability disclosure and patch cadence?
[06:22] Marcus: Yes, we publish a security page with patch cadence and a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy. For enterprise we can provide recent pen-test summaries and remediation timelines.
[06:32] Marta: From a legal perspective, where is the control plane hosted for Hosted? If data residency matters we need to know if logs or metadata leave EU.
[06:40] Marcus: We have regional control planes and data plane placements. For strict EU residency we recommend Private or Dedicated with region pinning. Hosted may have EU regions but certain control plane features are centralized, we should map those specifics in the follow-up doc.
[06:57] Jonas: On the model side — do you let us pin model versions and restrict model upgrades? We don't want silent rollouts that change LLM behavior unexpectedly.
[07:05] Marcus: Absolutely. Rollouts are pin-able per route and we support canary and A/B tests. Automatic model updates are opt-in only for enterprise customers.
[07:16] Elise: Regarding logging again — chain of custody is important. Can we get signed logs or an append-only ledger for admin actions?
[07:24] Marcus: We offer tamper-evident logs for enterprise customers; they can be pushed to your SIEM or S3 with integrity checks. For the highest assurance we recommend Private with local log retention.
[07:36] Lena: Quick check — do you have any hard deadlines or procurement timelines we should be aware of?
[07:41] Ravi: We're targeting a pilot in July and a production cutover in Q4. Legal needs BAAs and SOC2 artifacts sooner rather than later.
[07:49] Marta: Yes please send SOC2, pen test summary and the BAA template so our counsel can review.
[07:55] Lena: Will do. Marcus will also share the network diagram.
[08:00] Marcus: One technical note — for GPU-backed inference we do KV cache and prefix caching to accelerate generation. For PHI paths we recommend disabling prefix cache, and use batching controls to balance latency and cost.
[08:15] Jonas: How does batching affect latency? We have sub-200ms requirements for some endpoints.
[08:20] Marcus: Batching helps throughput but adds queuing latency. For sub-200ms we can dedicate capacity and tune batching to small sizes or single-request fast paths. That's why Dedicated is usually chosen for strict latency SLOs.
[08:35] Elise: For auditability, can we run synthetic prompts and have deterministic logs for regression testing?
[08:43] Marcus: Yes, we support eval harnesses and test prompts. We can tie regressions to model and runtime versions and create alerts if quality drifts.
[08:54] Ravi: Does Redwood have any customers in healthcare we can reference?
[08:58] Lena: We have several healthcare customers; I'll provide references that are cleared for introductions.
[09:04] Elise: Any talk about data minimization — can Redwood do field-level redaction?
[09:09] Marcus: Yes field-level masking is supported via ingestion hooks or at the agent level. For unstructured text we have regex redactors and token filters; best to do it pre-ingestion inside your VPC.
[09:22] Jonas: On the ops side, what's the upgrade window for security patches? We require critical patches within 48-72 hours.
[09:28] Marcus: For enterprise Dedicated we aim to patch critical CVEs within 72 hours; private on-prem is your ops team but we provide hotfixes and runbooks.
[09:38] Marta: Let's talk about encryption key rotation and escrow — do you support rotation without downtime?
[09:44] Marcus: With KMS-backed envelopes you can rotate master keys with minimal interruption; we support double-writing for a window to avoid downtime. For HSM appliances, rotation can require coordination but we have runbooks.
[09:58] Elise: Does Redwood's telemetry include payload content for model debugging?
[10:04] Marcus: Only if logging is enabled; by default our production hosting scrubs content for redaction. For debugging sessions we can set a temporary policy with explicit consent.
[10:18] Ravi: Any limitations on data residency with third-party model providers or model artifacts?
[10:24] Marcus: We provide curated open models; model weights are stored in secure blob stores and can be region-pinned for Private/Dedicated. Hosted uses region storage but may replicate for availability — we can restrict replication if required.
[10:38] Elise: Ok. I'd like to map three scenarios: 1) Hosted enterprise with BAA, 2) Dedicated in EU region with BYOK, 3) Private on-prem. For each we need risk, controls, and estimated cost.
[10:51] Lena: We'll produce a comparison doc and include cost signals. Marcus will prepare the deployment diagram for scenario 2/3.
[10:58] Jonas: For benchmarking, what's the process? We can share a small representative workload and sequence length distribution.
[11:04] Marcus: Send sample payloads and we'd run a Dedicated benchmark on a reserved pool and share latency percentile and cost estimates. We'll need approx 2 weeks for a canonical run.
[11:14] Ravi: Any specific compliance questions we should put in our RFP?
[11:19] Marta: Please include: SOC2 Type II evidence, ISO mapping, BAA template, pen test summary, patch cadence, incident response contacts, data residency guarantees, and SAML/SCIM integration steps.
[11:31] Marcus: Noted — we'll include all that in the package.
[11:36] Elise: Do you have support for key escrow and emergency access procedures? We need to know about break-glass for legal holds.
[11:44] Marcus: Yes break-glass procedures exist for Dedicated/Private. They require multi-party approvals and are auditable. We'll send the doc.
[11:54] Lena: Great. Quick recap and owners: Lena sends SOC2 and references, Marcus sends architecture and KMS/HSM notes and benchmarking plan, Jonas will send sample payloads, Elise and Marta will consolidate legal/compliance questions.
[12:08] Ravi: That works. Thanks, all.
[12:12] Lena: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the package by end of week.

End of transcript.
